quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 financial report, reported (IFRS) figures: Q2 2026 net sales DKK 78,488 million rose 3% at CER, held back by a DKK 2.6 billion 340B rebate provision reversal in Q2 2025; reported operating profit DKK 27,061 million fell 16% at CER, hit by non-cash impairment charges of DKK 6.3 billion on intangible pipeline assets including monlunabant (DKK 4.0 billion), booked in R&D costs; net profit fell 21% to DKK 20,989 million. H1 2026 reported sales were DKK 175,311 million (+18% at CER), including a DKK 26.8 billion 340B sales rebate provision reversal in Q1 2026; H1 adjusted sales were DKK 148,551 million (+2% at CER) and adjusted operating profit DKK 66,247 million (+2% at CER).
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 reported sales DKK 78,488 million (+3% CER); reported operating profit DKK 27,061 million (-16% CER); impairments DKK 6.3 billion incl. monlunabant DKK 4.0 billion; net profit DKK 20,989 million (-21%); H1 adjusted sales DKK 148,551 million (+2%), adjusted operating profit DKK 66,247 million (+2%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 adjusted sales by brand: Wegovy injectable DKK 19,484 million (+1% at CER; US Operations down 22% on lower realised prices, International Operations up 46%); Wegovy pill DKK 3,218 million (US DKK 3,141 million; International Operations DKK 77 million, mainly wholesaler pipeline fill ahead of the first launch outside the US); Ozempic DKK 31,375 million (+5%); Ozempic pill / Rybelsus DKK 5,228 million (down 4%); Saxenda DKK 450 million (down 47%); total insulin DKK 12,941 million (+6%); Rare disease DKK 4,907 million (+6%), with rare endocrine disorders up 24%.

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 adjusted sales by region: International Operations DKK 37,619 million (+10% at CER) - EUCAN DKK 19,206 million (+17%), Emerging Markets DKK 8,413 million (+5%), APAC DKK 5,030 million (down 6%), Region China DKK 4,970 million (+13%); US Operations DKK 40,869 million (+4%). Lower Wegovy prices were mainly realised in Region China following list price reductions in late Q4 2025. By segment, Q2 operating profit was DKK 28,356 million in Obesity and Diabetes care (38.5% margin) and an operating loss of DKK 1,295 million in Rare disease (margin (26.4)%, versus a DKK 518 million profit in Q2 2025).
quarterly_data.figure: IO DKK 37,619 million (+10%); EUCAN DKK 19,206 million (+17%); EM DKK 8,413 million (+5%); APAC DKK 5,030 million; China DKK 4,970 million (+13%); Rare disease operating loss DKK 1,295 million

quarterly_data.signal: US commercial detail: Wegovy pill reached around 2.9 million total prescriptions in Q2 2026; it is available at over 70,000 pharmacies and through nine telehealth organisations, self-pay prices range from USD 149-299 per month by dose, and commercial formulary access is on par with injectable Wegovy. Injectable Wegovy weekly prescriptions were around 310,000 for the week ending 17 July, of which around 120,000 were self-pay. Wegovy HD (7.2 mg) received accelerated FDA approval in March under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot programme and launched nationwide on 7 April; the three largest PBMs added it to standard formularies as a line extension. Ozempic pill was made available nationwide on 4 May. Effective 1 October 2026, CVS Caremark will add other weight loss medications, in addition to Wegovy, to its largest commercial template formularies.
quarterly_data.figure: Wegovy pill ~2.9 million TRx in Q2; >70,000 pharmacies; nine telehealth organisations; USD 149-299 per month self-pay; injectable Wegovy ~310,000 weekly TRx (~120,000 self-pay); CVS Caremark formulary change effective 1 October 2026

quarterly_data.signal: US list price cut: effective 1 January 2027 Novo Nordisk will lower the list price (WAC) of Wegovy injection 2.4 mg and 7.2 mg and tablets up to 25 mg, Ozempic injection 0.5 mg, 1 mg and 2 mg, and Ozempic pill 7 mg or 14 mg to USD 675, reductions from the current list price of approximately 50% for Wegovy and 35% for Ozempic, applying to all doses; the change is expected to impact the company's cash flow in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: list price USD 675 from 1 January 2027; approximately 50% (Wegovy) and 35% (Ozempic) reductions

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook detail in the H1 report: the 4 August raise compares with 6 May 2026 guidance of -4% to -12% for both adjusted sales growth and adjusted operating profit growth at CER; on a non-adjusted basis the mid-points would be 5% and 12%. Free cash flow is now expected at DKK 45-55 billion (previously 36-46 bDKK); capital expenditure is still expected at around DKK 55 billion in 2026 versus DKK 60 billion in 2025, for API, aseptic production, finished production and packaging capacity, and is expected to decline in the coming years (H1 2026 capex DKK 24.0 billion versus DKK 28.1 billion). R&D spend and promotional activities are expected to increase in the second half versus the first half of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: prior guidance -4% to -12%; non-adjusted mid-points 5% and 12%; free cash flow DKK 45-55 billion (from 36-46); capex ~DKK 55 billion in 2026 vs DKK 60 billion in 2025; H1 capex DKK 24.0 billion

quarterly_data.signal: International rollout: more than 20 launches of Ozempic 2.0 mg are planned throughout 2026; Wegovy 7.2 mg in the single-dose pen received full EMA approval on 15 July (UK approval 14 April, UK availability since 1 June) with a broad rollout planned across more than 30 markets in International Operations in 2026; Wegovy is launched in around 60 countries.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 20 Ozempic 2.0 mg launches in 2026; Wegovy 7.2 mg rollout in more than 30 markets; Wegovy in around 60 countries

quarterly_data.signal: Further obesity and diabetes regulatory milestones in the H1 report: once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg (Wegovy) was approved for MASH with liver fibrosis stages F2 to F3 in Japan and the UK, based on part I of the ESSENCE trial; the US FDA accepted the filing to add ESSENCE MASH data to the Wegovy pill (oral semaglutide 25 mg) label, with a decision expected in Q1 2027; Japan and China's CDE approved the Rybelsus label update with SOUL cardiovascular outcomes data (14% reduction in MACE risk); the 25 mg dose of Ozempic pill was submitted to the FDA with a decision expected during Q4 2026. Approval data cited: OASIS 4 (Wegovy pill) 16.6% average weight loss with one in three reaching 20% or more; STEP UP (Wegovy 7.2 mg) 20.7% average weight loss with around one-third reaching 25% or more; SUSTAIN OPTIMIZE (Ozempic 2.0 mg add-on to dose-reduced insulin glargine) -1.4% mean HbA1c and -8.0kg mean weight versus dose-titrated insulin glargine.
quarterly_data.figure: MASH approvals Japan and UK; Wegovy pill MASH FDA decision Q1 2027; SOUL label Japan and China (MACE -14%); Ozempic pill 25 mg FDA decision Q4 2026; OASIS 4 16.6%; STEP UP 20.7%; SUSTAIN OPTIMIZE -1.4% HbA1c, -8.0kg

quarterly_data.signal: Rare disease regulatory milestones: Sogroya was approved in Japan (and recommended by the CHMP in the EU) for children with short stature born small for gestational age and with Noonan Syndrome, based on REAL 8 and REAL 9; Novo submitted Turner Syndrome in the EU, with a Turner Syndrome decision expected in Q4 2026 in the US and in the first half of 2027 in the EU and Japan. Denecimig was submitted to China's CDE for haemophilia A based on the FRONTIER programme. Alhemo (concizumab) paediatric label extensions were submitted in Japan and the US. Etavopivat's HIBISCUS phase 3 trial was completed, meeting both co-primary endpoints.
quarterly_data.figure: Sogroya Japan approval (SGA, Noonan); Turner Syndrome decisions Q4 2026 US, H1 2027 EU and Japan; denecimig China submission; Alhemo paediatric submissions; HIBISCUS met both co-primary endpoints

quarterly_data.signal: Clinical results in the H1 report: in REIMAGINE 4, evaluating the effects if all people adhered to treatment, tirzepatide 15 mg achieved a weight loss of 15.8% and an HbA1c reduction of 2.2 percentage points at 68 weeks (CagriSema 2.4 mg/2.4 mg: 15.2% and 1.9 percentage points). The UBT251 phase 2 trial in China was successfully completed. The GSI (NN1644) phase 1 trial was completed with all multiple doses appearing safe and well tolerated, and further development will be assessed. The Inno8 phase 1 trial in healthy male participants was completed with all doses appearing safe and well tolerated; a phase 1 in people with haemophilia A is ongoing. Novo terminated the monlunabant development project due to portfolio considerations.
quarterly_data.figure: REIMAGINE 4 tirzepatide 15 mg: 15.8% weight loss, HbA1c -2.2 percentage points at 68 weeks; monlunabant terminated

quarterly_data.signal: Trial initiations and readout timing in the H1 report: the CagriSema 2.4 mg/7.2 mg REDEFINE high-dose phase 3 trial is expected to read out in the first half of 2028. The zenagamtide AMAZE phase 3 programme was initiated, including HF-POLARIS (subcutaneous zenagamtide vs placebo on morbidity and mortality in heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction and obesity; approximately 5600 patients; event-driven; readout second half of 2029) and AMAZE 8 (zenagamtide vs semaglutide on body weight in overweight or obesity with type 2 diabetes, two years of exposure; readout first half of 2029). The Triple phase 2 dose-finding trial enrols around 230 people with readout expected in the first quarter of 2027; the UBT251 phase 2 enrols around 300 people. Phase 1 starts: ACSL5i; NNC0497-0040 in type 1 diabetes (146 people, readout second half of 2028); oral NLRP3 inhibitor NNC6022-0004 (readout second half of 2027). Expected: oral zenagamtide phase 3 initiation in Q3 2026; subcutaneous zenagamtide cardiovascular outcomes phase 3 and cagrilintide high-dose phase 3 initiations in Q4 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: REDEFINE high-dose readout H1 2028; HF-POLARIS ~5600 patients, readout H2 2029; AMAZE 8 readout H1 2029; Triple phase 2 ~230 people, readout Q1 2027; UBT251 phase 2 ~300 people; NNC0497-0040 146 people, H2 2028; NLRP3 phase 1 readout H2 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Legal matters in the H1 report: Cipla filed an ANDA with Paragraph IV certifications for a generic Ozempic and Novo Nordisk filed a patent infringement complaint against Cipla in the Federal Court for the District of New Jersey; on 30 June 2026 Sandoz AG filed suit in the Unified Patent Court (Milan Central Division) seeking revocation of Novo's Unitary Patent 3 689 365 covering the 1mg semaglutide dose for diabetes in 18 EU countries, which Novo says it is fully prepared to defend; on 21 July 2026 Novo sued Eli Lilly in New Jersey federal court alleging false advertising over comparative-efficacy direct-to-consumer campaigns; and on 18 May 2026 the US Supreme Court denied Novo's petition in its Inflation Reduction Act pricing challenge, closing that matter.
quarterly_data.figure: Cipla ANDA (Paragraph IV) for generic Ozempic; Sandoz UPC revocation suit on semaglutide 1mg patent in 18 EU countries; Lilly false-advertising suit; IRA challenge closed
